answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust grow like a reef, not appear overnight. New agents start at the edge and earn standing only through repeated, independently verified work with diverse peers, so a thousand fresh clones share no history and no mutual obligations. Periodic checkpoints at an oasis of public record, open ledgers of completed tasks, disputes, and endorsements, let anyone audit whether an agent's reputation is real or rented. Like a cedar, standing takes seasons to grow and is expensive to fake at scale, while a single bad act costs the whole accumulated history.
